source.title: ConceptTracer: Interactive Analysis of Concept Saliency and Selectivity in Neural Representations
source.authors: Ricardo Knauer; A. Beinrucker; Erik Rodner

record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron–concept associations using saliency and selectivity to investigate neuron interpretability, but it does not directly test whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs.
record.gate_note: The reported task AUCs do not measure neuron polysemanticity. The comparisons with SHAP and optimal probing are not results about the neurons’ own behavior. The study does report neuron–concept association measurements and examples; these are recorded as findings about the claim’s subject, but they do not measure any listed version directly.
record.test_reason: The paper presents a tool (ConceptTracer) and demonstrates it on TabPFN, a tabular transformer, measuring neuron–concept saliency and selectivity. It never measures whether neurons respond to several unrelated inputs. It does not study vision classifiers or language-model MLP neurons. It does not test superposition, training or architecture effects, or measurement dependence of polysemanticity. It mentions superposed representations only in related work. The record's 'tests/T2' is wrong: the results bear on neuron–concept association, not on any version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say ConceptTracer supports identifying interpretable neurons in TabPFN and exploring how it encodes concepts. They add that exhaustive search beats sparse probing for finding the most selective pairs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses normalized mutual information for concept saliency and a normalized share of a neuron's total saliency for selectivity, rather than the original sources' methods. It analyzes TabPFN tabular representations.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that selectivity depends on the size of the concept set; they also report different selectivity clusters for low/mid-level versus high-level ICD concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: In TabPFN 6.3.2 embeddings across 24 layers, fewer than 1% of neurons are significantly salient and selective for ICD concepts. Pareto-front neurons appear in initial, middle and final layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In tabular foundation models, few individual neurons are selectively associated with predefined clinical concepts, and such neurons are not concentrated in particular layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Example neurons show differentiation among related subconcepts (neuron 162, layer 0) and integration across related features (neuron 145, layer 22).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-selective neurons in tabular models can either split or merge related input concepts.

record.problems: The study analyzes only TabPFN on one tabular dataset and uses a predefined, filtered ICD concept set. Saliency/selectivity for those concepts does not directly establish whether mixed neuron responses are unrelated; the reported less-than-1% figure is not broken down by task. Selectivity is acknowledged to depend on concept-set size.
record.rows_left_out: The plotted numerical coordinates and individual neuron–concept points in Figure 2 were not separately extracted; the figure-only task-level results are recorded in r4–r7. Task AUCs and sparse-probing baseline comparisons were left out because they do not measure the claim's subject.

untested.parts: No language models; TabPFN target-column embeddings only, and polysemantic share not measured.
Initialization, regularization and noise are not varied.
Only one model is studied, with no architecture or activation comparison.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not revisited.
Selectivity's dependence on concept-set size is noted by construction, but polysemanticity classification across measurement choices is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool/demo paper whose own contribution is the method. Related-work mention of superposition is citation only. The relation should be discusses or cites_only at most, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses TabPFN on tabular data, not image classifiers, and does not test responses to multiple unrelated image inputs.
No transformer language models, MLP neurons, or token/context responses are studied.
The study does not test superposition or whether feature count exceeds neuron count.
The study does not vary initialization, regularization, or training noise, or test capacity pressure.
Only TabPFN is analyzed; activation functions, architectures, regularization, and performance trade-offs are not compared.
The study does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons or establish how often apparently mixed responses share a feature. Its examples concern related ICD concepts in a tabular model.
It notes that selectivity depends on the size of the concept set, but does not compare activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods to test when neurons count as polysemantic.

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron–concept saliency and selectivity with permutation testing.

conditions.value: inhospital mortality, ICU transfer within 12h, critical outcome, and hospitalization; reported together

rows.measure: Fraction of neurons significantly salient and selective for specific concepts
rows.baseline: Permutation-based empirical null; no numerical baseline stated
rows.note: The text does not disaggregate the less-than-1% result by task. This measures concept association, not whether responses to multiple concepts are unrelated.
rows.check: Under 1% of neurons are significantly salient and selective. This is a monosemantic-detection rate on a filtered ICD concept set, not a rate of polysemanticity. A low rate does not imply the other neurons are polysemantic. The model is a tabular transformer, not a language-model MLP.

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2, neuron 162 in layer 0
rows.operation_detail: Compared saliency and selectivity for ICD concepts E87 and E86.
rows.measure: Saliency and selectivity for the concepts
rows.value: For E86, saliency and selectivity are reduced by 0.12 and 0.03, respectively
rows.note: The authors describe E87 as a salient and selective response and the reduced response to E86 as differentiation within a composite input feature.
rows.check: This is a single-neuron example of differentiation between related ICD subconcepts. It is a demo, not a polysemanticity measurement.

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2, neuron 145 in layer 22
rows.operation_detail: Measured mutual information between neuron activations and features conditioned on ICD code I being present.
rows.measure: Rank of cardiac arrhythmias and hypertension by mutual information with the neuron's activations
rows.value: Both rank among the top 4 features
rows.note: The authors characterize this as integration across related input features.
rows.check: This is an example of integration across related features (cardiac conditions within ICD I). These are related concepts, not unrelated ones, so it bears on no version.

rows.subject: TabPFN 6.3.2
rows.operation_detail: Plotted significant neuron–concept pairs by saliency and selectivity.
rows.measure: Saliency and selectivity of significant neuron–concept pairs and their Pareto front
rows.note: The plot does not establish whether any multiple concept associations are unrelated.
rows.check: Figure only. Pareto fronts are partly the tool's comparison against SHAP and optimal-probing baselines, i.e. the study's own method versus others.
